text:
Alex: Kickoff thread for BlueRidge Irrigation POC. They need streaming SDK + function-calls that output Protobuf-encoded events to a legacy event gateway. Big asks: SAML SSO, bring-your-own KMS for embeddings, and a cost estimate for ~8k steady QPS with 3x burst. Any obvious red flags?
Priya: Noted. Quick checklist: 1) Python streaming example that shows reconnect/backoff 2) function_call -> Protobuf serializer + schema registry guidance 3) Dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs for predictable tail latency.
Rafael: I can prototype the serializer. They insisted on Protobuf v3 with a compact schema (message SensorReading { string id = 1; double val = 2; map<string,string> meta = 3; }). Need to confirm max payload size and whether returning base64 binary inside the protobuf is OK.
Alex: They asked about region failover: EU primary, US DR. Sales wants a ballpark for reserved capacity pricing and a hosted fallback plan.
Priya: For embeddings encryption: Dedicated supports customer CMK (we can rotate), Hosted uses our managed key but we can do envelope encryption on enterprise plan. I'll link the presales KMS doc.
ops-bot: Presales docs -> <https://redwood.example.com/docs/presales/kms-keys|KMS: customer-managed keys> :link: 
Rafael: Draft Python streaming snippet (simple):
```python
from redwood import StreamingClient
client = StreamingClient(region='eu')
with client.stream(model='redwood-compact') as s:
    for msg in s.receive():
        if msg.type == 'function_call':
            # msg.payload is JSON string from model's structured output
            event = protobuf_serialize(parse(msg.payload))
            post_to_gateway(event)
```
Priya: Add exponential backoff on reconnects and jitter; also show how to surface telemetry for dropped messages. They have flaky LTE field gateways.
Alex: Rafael, can the serializer produce directly a binary protobuf buffer so they can POST with content-type application/x-protobuf?
Rafael: Yes. We'll show both base64-in-json and direct binary POST. Recommend direct binary to avoid token inflation if model returns large blobs. But warn about multipart uploads for large images.
Priya: Also add a tiny Rust example because their infra team prefers Rust for the gateway. Keep it minimal.
Rafael: Rust sketch (pseudo):
```rust
// pseudo-code
let mut stream = redwood::Stream::open("redwood-compact");
while let Some(msg) = stream.next().await {
  if msg.kind == FunctionCall {
    let payload = parse_json(&msg.payload);
    let pb = sensor::SensorReading::from(payload);
    http::post("https://events.bridge.local", pb.to_bytes());
  }
}
```
Priya: For capacity: Devon from infra suggested Dedicated pools with autoscale + burst. For 8k steady, estimate 3-5 A10 equivalents depending on model latency. I'll ask infra for a tighter GPU count once Alex shares model prompt lengths and max output tokens.
Alex: Action items: (1) Rafael to drop Python + Rust adapters and Protobuf snippet; (2) Priya to draft a two-option pricing: reserved pool vs hosted with burst fallback; (3) Rafael to confirm binary size limits and recommend signed-URL pattern for >2MB blobs.
ops-bot: Link -> <https://redwood.example.com/docs/presales/streaming-best-practices|Streaming best practices>
Rafael: Security questionnaire note: they sent a short questionnaire focused on network isolation, key rotation, and data residency. I'll collate answers and mark any items needing SecOps review.
Priya: On the SSO front: we support SAML IdP for Console + Service-accounts can be provisioned for CI. For private deployments we can offer VPC peering or private link.
Alex: Quick question from customer: can function_call responses include signed URLs instead of embedding binary? They prefer signed URLs to keep events small.
Rafael: Strongly recommend signed URLs. We'll include helper to generate pre-signed upload URLs and an example flow: model returns attachment_url in function_call, client fetches and stores. Mention expiry and egress implications.
Alex: Great. I'll schedule a tech call with BlueRidge SecOps for Monday. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
